# Automations and Scripts Catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_automation_catalog.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every Home Assistant automation and script defined in this repo, with the
`description:` field from its YAML. Private packages are listed under their
`private_templates/*.tmpl` source and rendered with the synthetic example
values, so placeholder names such as `example_zone_05` stand in for private ones.

Totals: **259 automations** and **162 scripts** across 50 files.

To keep this current, add a `description:` to every new automation or script
and regenerate:

```bash
uv run python scripts/generate_automation_catalog.py
```

`tests/test_automation_script_descriptions.py` fails when a description is
missing or this file is stale. Topic docs in `docs/` and the Allium specs in
`specs/` hold the deeper behavior notes for each area.

## `private_templates/adaptive_lighting.yaml.tmpl`

### Automations

| ID | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reconcile_owner_suite_adaptive_lighting` | reconcile_owner_suite_adaptive_lighting | single | Reapply the Adaptive Lighting baselines after Home Assistant starts so kitchen, laundry-room, den, basement, dining-room, owner-suite, and vanity tuning survives restarts while preserving each room's intended scene and task-lighting behavior. The runtime dining-room Adaptive Lighting switch now uses the current dining-room entity id. The bed strip has its own switch so Adaptive Lighting itself holds it at bed_strip_automatic_max_brightness_percent; a cap automation that re-sent brightness was marked as a manual override and paused the whole owner suite. |
| `clear_hallway_adaptive_sleep_mode_when_house_sleep_ends` | clear_hallway_adaptive_sleep_mode_when_house_sleep_ends | restart | Explicitly release the hallway Adaptive Lighting sleep profile when the house sleep group turns off. The hallway sleep switch is currently a member of that UI-managed group, but this cleanup keeps the garage-entry safety path correct if group membership changes and after a restart. |
| `apply_adaptive_lighting_on_arrival` | apply_adaptive_lighting_on_arrival | single | Instantly correct color temperature and brightness for any lights that turn on as part of home-arrival automations. Fires for all transport modes (car, Uber, Lyft, walking) via the Bayesian presence sensor. A 2-second delay lets arrival-scene transitions begin before the adaptive apply fires. Empty-house arrivals can apply across all configured arrival switches; occupied-house arrivals only apply to configured lights that Adaptive Lighting has not marked as manually controlled. If the bed is occupied, only common-area arrival switches are eligible so the owner suite is not disturbed. Arrival only applies to switches that are already enabled; turn_on_lights=false keeps off lights undisturbed. Resolves #486. |
| `nightly_adaptive_lighting_cycle_reset` | nightly_adaptive_lighting_cycle_reset | single | Every 4 hours, cycle every main adaptive lighting switch off then back on to unstick color or brightness matching that has drifted. A startup trigger acts as a recovery path: if HA restarts during the 10-second off window the next boot immediately re-enables all switches so they are never stranded off. Control switches (sleep_mode, adapt_brightness, adapt_color) are excluded to preserve their settings. |

### Scripts

| Script | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `script.adaptive_light_turn_on` | Adaptive Light Turn On | parallel | Turn on Adaptive Lighting-managed lights with one atomic adaptive apply so brightness and color cannot arrive as competing Zigbee commands. Optional reset/ramp callers may lock manual control until their transition finishes; lights the user overrides mid-ramp retain that lock. Falls back to a plain light.turn_on when the Adaptive Lighting switch is unavailable so wall switches and motion paths keep working. |
| `script.adaptive_light_clear_manual_control` | Adaptive Light Clear Manual Control | parallel | Deferred, guarded manual-control clear for script.adaptive_light_turn_on. Waits out the brightness ramp, then clears the Adaptive Lighting manual-control marks only for lights the user did not override mid-ramp. Invoked non-blocking via script.turn_on with the variables adaptive_switch, clear_lights, and wait_seconds. |

## `packages/cleaning.yaml`

### Automations

| ID | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `washer_started` | washer_started | single | Mark the washer as actively running. |
| `wash_finished` | wash_finished | single | Start the finished-washer reminder sequence when washer power returns to standby. |
| `dryer_started` | dryer_started | single | Clear any prior dryer reminder when a new cycle starts. |
| `dryer_finished` | dryer_finished | single | Mark a dryer load ready for the next laundry-room entry. |
| `laundry_room_entry_reminder` | laundry_room_entry_reminder | single | Surface completed washer and dryer loads once when someone enters and turns on the laundry-room lights. The physical switch is the entry proxy because the room has no motion or occupancy entity. |
| `washer_reminder` | washer_reminder | single | Escalate a finished washer load after one hour without acknowledgement. |
| `washer_cleared` | washer_cleared | single | Reset the washer back to IDLE once the finished load has been handled or manually acknowledged. |
| `x40_vacuum_live_activity` | X40 Vacuum Live Activity | parallel | Lock-screen Live Activity on the Wethop iPhone tracking the X40 Ultra while it cleans the house. Starts/updates on state, room, and progress changes; shows complete then clears when it docks. mode: parallel (not queued): the terminal dock/completion branches read OTHER entities' live state (e.g. whether the two-stage orchestrator script has finished) to decide what to do, and mode: queued lets a trigger's own condition evaluation happen arbitrarily late — dequeued only once every earlier queued instance (including a 2-minute delay branch) has finished — by which point that state may have already moved on, defeating the check (Codex found this twice: first against a mode-select-based check, then again against the script-state check that replaced it). Under parallel, a trigger's instance starts essentially immediately, collapsing that window to ordinary async scheduling latency. Consecutive runs ARE possible despite that (x40_ultra_main_level_policy_clean is itself mode: queued, so a request accumulated during a long run starts the instant the first docks — observed in practice: the daily litter segment starting 13 seconds after a trip's full-floor pass docked) — so every delayed clear_notification below re-checks that the vacuum hasn't started cleaning again before firing, rather than assuming completion events never overlap. |
| `washer_live_activity` | Washer Live Activity | queued | Lock-screen Live Activity on the Wethop iPhone for the washing machine. Shows phase + progress while running (CLEANING), persists as an unload reminder through CLEAN/REMINDED, flags MUSTY, and clears when emptied (IDLE). Keyed off input_select.washer_state. |
| `dryer_live_activity` | Dryer Live Activity | queued | Lock-screen Live Activity on the Wethop iPhone for the dryer. Shows phase + progress while running; shows complete then clears when the cycle ends. |


## `private_templates/climate.yaml.tmpl`

### Automations

| ID | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `buy_more_air_filters` | buy_more_air_filters | single | Prompt for a filter count when the inventory is empty and we are either standing in a DIY store or just back from an errand. The store path leans on sensor.diy_store_current, whose state is which store we are at, rather than matching place-name strings directly; see packages/zone.yaml for why exact matching kept missing. Triggering on the identity rather than a boolean is what lets a second store in one trip prompt while a second fix for the same store does not. The arrival path exists because that store signal can miss entirely: Places only re-geocodes on a new GPS fix, so parking in a big-box lot resolves to the lot and the phone then reports nothing for the whole visit. Asking on the way home is the backstop for that case. |
| `air_filters_purchased` | air_filters_purchased | single | Record the number of air filters purchased from the phone notification reply into the air-filter inventory helper. |
| `toggle_bathroom_fan_when_showering` | toggle_bathroom_fan_when_showering | parallel | Run each shower bathroom's exhaust fan while its humidity-high sensor is on and turn it off when humidity returns to normal. |
| `window_climate_action_handler` | window_climate_action_handler | queued | Handle phone notification actions for the open-window climate prompts: pause or resume the thermostat, or ignore/keep paused. |
| `window_climate_open_prompt` | window_climate_open_prompt | single | Prompt the resident to pause the thermostat after a window has been open for 5 minutes (with a 2-hour follow-up) while home and the thermostat is running. |
| `window_climate_resume_prompt` | window_climate_resume_prompt | single | Prompt the resident to resume the thermostat after all windows have been closed for an hour (with a 4-hour follow-up) when climate was paused for windows. |

## `packages/parasoll_fix.yaml`

### Automations

| ID | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parasoll_auto_reconfigure_on_join` | PARASOLL - Auto-Reconfigure on Join or Announce | queued | Reconfigures PARASOLL sensors only when the Z2M bridge/devices state shows a gap. Four invariants are checked on every trigger: • ssIasZone bound on ep2 — device will send contact-state reports • genPollCtrl NOT bound on ep1 — no aggressive check-in → no battery drain • genPowerCfg has configured reportings — battery/voltage actively reported • max reporting interval ≤ 14400 s on zoneStatus + battery attrs — device reports often enough to never be marked offline (the actual drop-off fix; without it the factory 65000 s default applies) Triggers: • device_interview — brand-new join (always reconfigures; no bindings yet) • device_announce — re-join / reboot (reconfigures only if bridge shows gap) • contact_change — PARASOLL state change (reconfigures only if bridge shows genPollCtrl bound or power reporting absent; active contact report already proves IAS zone is enrolled) Rate limit: the first action stops the run if this device had a configure attempt within the last hour, so a rejoin-looping or repeatedly-failing sensor can trigger at most one configure/hour instead of flooding the coordinator with binds (the failure mode that took the network down). Notifications gated by 1 h since last successful configure per device; contact_change is always silent. |

### Scripts

| Script | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `script.parasoll_enforce_intervals` | PARASOLL - Enforce Reporting Intervals | parallel | Sets maximum_report_interval = 14400 s on ssIasZone/zoneStatus (ep2), genPowerCfg/batteryPercentageRemaining (ep1) and genPowerCfg/batteryVoltage (ep1) for a single PARASOLL sensor, identified by IEEE address. Mins and reportable changes are left at the herdsman-converters factory values (zoneStatus min 0; battery min 3600, change 10). |
| `script.parasoll_reconfigure_all` | PARASOLL - Reconfigure All | single | For every joined PARASOLL sensor: presses the identify button to nudge the device awake, then sends a Z2M reconfigure command so the stock converter settings (ssIasZone binding, no genPollCtrl) are applied, and clamps the reporting intervals to 14400 s. Commands are queued by Z2M for sleepy devices and processed on the next check-in. Sensors that are completely dead still need a battery pull first. |

The 06:00 start is the normal schedule only; while guest mode is on, catnip_grow_light_reconcile owns the guest window (11:00-22:00) so the 260W fixture stays off overnight and through the morning while guests are staying. |

A periodic sweep covers every such gap without needing a dedicated trigger for each way the switch can miss a transition. Also reacts immediately to guest_mode changes and to any state report from the switch itself (recovering from unavailable, first registration, or a manual toggle). Basement/Grow Light sits in the unfinished basement (docs/room_intent.yaml): with guests staying it may run during the day but must be off from 22:00 to 11:00, so guest mode narrows the desired window to 11:00-22:00 instead of the normal 06:00-24:00. A trip guest visit keeps it off entirely, as before. |

## `packages/sleep_quality.yaml`

### Automations

| ID | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sleep_quality_prepare_session` | Sleep quality - prepare session | queued | Record the most recent nightly bed entry, then start a persistent session after sustained CPAP use without changing existing goodnight behavior. |
| `sleep_quality_track_active_session` | Sleep quality - track active session | queued | Count bed transitions during CPAP use, persist a guarded CPAP stop, and finalize once the aggregate owner-suite bed is empty. |
| `sleep_quality_reconcile_cpap_stop_after_restart` | Sleep quality - reconcile CPAP stop after restart | single | A pending numeric_state/state `for:` debounce (cpap_start, cpap_stop, or bed_exit, above) is discarded on an HA restart *or* an automation reload — it does not resume merely because the underlying condition stays true, only if the entity changes state again (Codex P2 follow-up on #373: a plain reload doesn't emit homeassistant.start, so that alone missed the reload case). Three independent debounces can each be lost this way, so all three are reconciled here, in order: (1) if CPAP was already running before the gap and its own 10-second debounce never got to run, no session ever started; (2) if CPAP had already dropped before the gap and its stop debounce never ran, sleep_session_cpap_stopped is stuck off; (3) if CPAP's own debounce already completed (cpap_stopped is on) but the bed's separate bed_exit debounce was the one in flight when the gap hit, sleep_session_bed_out is left stale. Each branch re-checks its underlying condition has held for the SAME full debounce duration the normal trigger requires, not just its instantaneous state, so a reload moments after a genuine transition can't fast-track past a debounce a normal trigger would still be waiting out (Codex P2 follow-up on #373). That per-branch `for:` guard created a second gap on a real restart (not just a reload): HA resets a restored entity's last_changed to the restore moment, so the guard's duration requirement almost never reads as satisfied on the one-shot homeassistant.start evaluation, and with no delayed or state-triggered follow-up the reconciliation was simply missed (Codex P2 follow-up on #373). Re-check periodically instead of only once: a state's `for:` duration is measured from whenever it last actually changed, so as long as it stays unchanged, a later periodic evaluation naturally satisfies the same guard once enough real time has elapsed since the restore/reload — recovering the debounce without needing to know or trust the original, pre-restart transition time. |

### Scripts

| Script | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `script.sleep_quality_rearm_cpap_resume` | Sleep quality - re-arm CPAP resume | single | Bank the interruption that just ended into accumulated active time, start a fresh segment at resume_timestamp, and clear the stop latch. Routed through this single mode: single script so the live cpap_resume trigger (in sleep_quality_track_active_session) and the periodic reconciliation re-arm (in sleep_quality_reconcile_cpap_stop_after_restart) can't both observe sleep_session_cpap_stopped as "on" and independently bank the same interruption — mode: single means a concurrent second call is dropped outright while the first is still running, and the internal state check below still protects a call that starts only after the first has already finished (Codex P2 follow-up on #373: serialize concurrent CPAP resume recovery). |
| `script.finalize_sleep_quality_session` | Finalize sleep quality session | single | Persist the latest owner-suite bed/CPAP durations and bounded continuity heuristic after both CPAP and bed occupancy have stopped. |

| `return_home_from_parents` | return_home_from_parents | single | On Sundays, resume the thermostat program and notify everyone when the resident leaves the family visit zone. |
| `send_nest_airport_home_eta` | send_nest_airport_home_eta | single | When flying home today, resume the thermostat program and notify everyone with an ETA as the resident leaves the airport. |
| `vacation_lights_on` | vacation_lights_on | single | During trip mode, turn on a random vacation lighting scene at sunset to simulate occupancy. |
| `vacation_lights_off` | vacation_lights_off | single | During trip mode, turn off the vacation lights and fans at the randomized off time and rerun the leave-home transition. |
| `vacuum_on_trip` | vacuum_on_trip | single | Run one full-floor pass on the main and upstairs levels during trips. |
| `vacuum_flying_home` | vacuum_flying_home | single | Start the flying-home clean far enough ahead that it is FINISHED input_number.pre_arrival_clean_buffer_minutes (default 30) before the plane lands: start = landing - input_number.pre_arrival_clean_lead_minutes (default 240 = worst measured X40 vacuum+mop cycle 191 min + the 30 min buffer + margin). Anchored to the flight's ARRIVAL (sensor.next_flight_home_arrival), not takeoff, because a cycle is longer than the flight; the house is empty for the whole trip so starting before takeoff is fine. A late start (late booking, HA restart, schedule change) degrades instead of running past the finish-by deadline: vacuum-only when at least 100 min remain, otherwise skipped with a notification. Launches once per landing (input_datetime.pre_arrival_clean_done_for), then confirms the upstairs and den robots really started (script.pre_arrival_confirm_secondary_robots). vacuum_flying_home_recover retries once if the X40 part ends unfinished. The replaced trigger was takeoff (binary_sensor.flying_home_today), which on 2026-10-09 finished the clean 49 min after landing. |
| `vacuum_flying_home_recover` | vacuum_flying_home_recover | single | One retry for a flying-home clean whose main-level (X40) part ended unfinished. On 2026-10-26 the X40 dropped off the Dreame cloud mid-vacuum and its task status lagged the dock by 3 s, so the run ended with no mop and nothing noticed. Fires when the X40 dispatcher goes idle, or after an HA restart (which kills the running script; a robot still physically running is left alone by the at-rest checks below). Decides from what actually finished since the clean started (input_datetime.x40_ultra_last_vacuumed_at / x40_ultra_last_mopped_at), planning against the finish-by deadline (landing - input_number.pre_arrival_clean_buffer_minutes): vacuum missing -> full cycle or vacuum-only, whichever still fits; only the mop missing (and owed) -> a mop-only pass if it fits; otherwise notify what is missing. Once per landing (input_datetime.pre_arrival_clean_retry_for). |
| `trip_guest_door_unlock_open_house` | trip_guest_door_unlock_open_house | restart | While on a trip and away, unlocking the (virtual) front door lock means a guest is checking on the cats: turn the water main back on and disarm the alarm, and remember the visit so the relock can undo it. |
| `trip_guest_door_lock_close_house` | trip_guest_door_lock_close_house | restart | When the front door locks again after a guest visit during a trip, turn the water main back off and re-arm the alarm. Only acts if the unlock automation started a visit, so it never re-arms on the owner's own return. Also runs at Home Assistant start so a restart mid-close (or with a restored visit flag and a locked door) reconciles the secured state. |
| `trip_guest_visit_clear_on_return` | trip_guest_visit_clear_on_return | single | Clears the guest-visit flag when the owner returns home or trip mode ends, so a visit left open mid-trip cannot re-arm the alarm or shut the water off on a later lock event. |

### Scripts

| Script | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `script.resume_ecobee_program_for_return_home` | resume_ecobee_program_for_return_home | queued | Resume the Ecobee program when a return-home travel signal fires. |
| `script.trip_vacuum_main_and_upstairs_levels` | trip_vacuum_main_and_upstairs_levels | queued | Run trip-safe whole-floor vacuuming and send the travel notification. |
| `script.pre_arrival_confirm_secondary_robots` | Confirm Pre-Arrival Upstairs And Den Robots Started | single | The upstairs START is a fire-and-forget MQTT publish and the den start can be vetoed by its own guards, so neither reports a failure; on 2026-10-26 neither robot ran during the pre-landing clean. Give each robot 3 min to show it is cleaning, re-send a start once (through the same guarded scripts), then notify which robot did not start and why. The upstairs robot is tracked on its Valetudo MQTT status topic (the trusted channel; the upstairs HA vacuum entity is unreliable, see vacuum_upstairs_segment_guarded); the den on vacuum.valetudo_den. Both finish well inside the X40 cycle (upstairs <=72 min, den <=30 min), so a late start still lands in time. |

The trigger ignores the unknown/unavailable -> error transition the entity makes while reconnecting after a restart, so a reboot never auto-starts the den robot. |
| `x40_ultra_maintenance_clean_after_four_home_days` | x40_ultra_maintenance_clean_after_four_home_days | single | Run a daily main-level maintenance clean at 13:00 once the house has stayed occupied for four days, so floors still get cleaned even without an away trigger. Main level only (the X40) — it does NOT start the upstairs robot, to avoid running bedroom/guest-area vacuums at 13:00 while someone is home. Does NOT force a mop: the policy vacuums every run and mops only when due (mop pending, or last successful mop >= 3 days old), so this fires daily but mops roughly every three days instead of every day. |
| `x40_ultra_record_home_since` | x40_ultra_record_home_since | single | Persist the timestamp the house last became home (start of the current home streak) so the four-home-days maintenance clean measures real occupancy and survives HA restarts. Set on the away->home edge; seeded once on startup if never recorded. A restart mid-streak keeps the existing value (the from:"off" trigger ignores the unknown->on transition at startup, and the startup seed only fires when the value is unset), so the streak is not reset. |
| `vacuum_laundry_room_daily_litter` | Vacuum laundry room daily (litter pickup) | single | Daily 1 PM vacuum-only clean of the laundry room (X40 map "Utility Room", segment 6) with three passes on Strong suction to pick up kitty litter. Routes through the single serialized policy entry (kind=segment), so it inherits the at-rest guard, the CleanGenius-off / sweeping-only guarantee (never mops), and the guest-mode veto. Because this is an AUTOMATIC launch, it additionally requires an empty bed (bayesian_bed_occupancy off) — matching the sibling 13:00 maintenance clean. |

### Scripts

| Script | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `script.vacuum_dock_all_robots` | Dock All Robot Vacuums | restart | Stop cleaning and return the den, main-level, and upstairs robots to their docks. Safe to call when a robot is already docked or unavailable. |
| `script.vacuum_den_guarded_start` | Start Den Vacuum (Guarded) | queued | Central boundary for den starts and error retries. Guest mode, a trip guest visit, or an open/unknown den door all fail closed. |
| `script.x40_ultra_prepare_deterministic_cleaning` | X40 Ultra Prepare Deterministic Cleaning | queued | Turn CleanGenius off so the cleaning-mode select becomes controllable. CleanGenius and manual cleaning-mode/customized-cleaning control are mutually exclusive on this device: while CleanGenius is active the cleaning-mode select and customized-cleaning switch are `unavailable`. Callers restore CleanGenius with x40_ultra_restore_cleangenius. |
| `script.x40_ultra_restore_cleangenius` | X40 Ultra Restore CleanGenius | queued | Restore CleanGenius to Deep cleaning after a deterministic policy run so manual/app-initiated cleans keep the user's default behavior. The select can briefly recover as off and become unavailable again while the dock finishes post-clean work, so wait for stable availability, retry the request, and fail visibly if the postcondition never becomes true. |
| `script.x40_ultra_wait_until_docked` | X40 Ultra Wait Until Docked | queued | Block until an already-running X40 truly finishes. Completion is judged on the vacuum entity only: mid-task mop washes read as `cleaning`, low-battery recharges read as `paused`, and rewash returns read as `returning`, so the entity reaches `docked`/`idle` only when the whole run (including any rewash/recharge) is done. Call this ONLY after confirming the run actually started, otherwise the entity is already docked and this waits the full timeout for a transition that never comes. |
| `script.x40_ultra_main_level_vacuum_only` | X40 Ultra Main Level Vacuum Only | queued | Sweep-only pass across the main level. Disables CleanGenius, forces the cleaning mode to sweeping, cleans the mapped main floor, then always restores CleanGenius. Publishes a run-scoped completion latch (input_boolean.x40_ultra_vacuum_pass_completed): reset off at the start and set on only when THIS pass reaches a real `completed` finish, so the mop orchestrator can tell a genuine finish from a no-op/failed/arrival-docked run without trusting the ambient (possibly stale) task_status. |
| `script.x40_ultra_main_level_mop_after_vacuum` | X40 Ultra Main Level Mop After Vacuum | queued | Clean the main level as two distinct full passes: a complete sweep-only vacuum of the whole floor, then — only if that vacuum actually finished — a dedicated mop-only pass. Running the passes separately (instead of the interleaved "mopping_after_sweeping" mode) means all dry debris is picked up before any water is applied. Both child scripts are mode: queued and awaited, so the mop never starts until the vacuum pass has docked. The mop is gated on the vacuum reaching a real `completed` task status: an arrival mid-run (vacuum_return_home -> return_to_base) or a rejected/no-op start docks the robot WITHOUT `completed`, so the mop is skipped and the mop debt is left pending to retry next run — this preserves both the arrival-to-dock protection and the vacuum-before-water ordering. x40_ultra_main_level_mop_only owns the persistent mop-schedule bookkeeping. The Live Activity notification (packages/cleaning.yaml) reads this script's OWN entity state (script.x40_ultra_main_level_mop_after_vacuum, 'on' for the full duration of both stages) to know a mop is queued behind the current vacuum pass, rather than a separately-tracked latch — so it is inherently correct across any kind of interruption (HA restart, script.reload, a manual stop) with no dedicated cleanup step of its own. Because the generic Live Activity completion branch therefore suppresses EVERY dock while this script is "on" (it cannot tell an interim dock from the final one without re-introducing the same staleness problem), THIS script is responsible for explicitly posting the outcome message on all three of its endings below (vacuum skipped, mop skipped/incomplete, or genuine success) the instant each is known — the interim dock in between gets no message of its own, which is correct: nothing is actually finished yet. The 2-minute wait-then-clear that used to follow each message here now lives in packages/cleaning.yaml instead, keyed off this script's own on->off transition: a delay INSIDE this script is exactly as reload-cancellable as the phase flag this script replaced, so script.reload firing mid-delay (packages/media_player.yaml calls it) would strand the notification forever with no clear ever firing. A delay living in the automation is immune to script.reload entirely. Also sets input_boolean.x40_ultra_orchestrated_run_active for the narrower case a script.reload doesn't cover: a full HA restart, which leaves no on->off transition for the Live Activity to observe at all. See that input_boolean's own declaration for how it's reconciled. |
| `script.x40_ultra_main_level_mop_only` | X40 Ultra Main Level Mop Only | queued | Mop-only pass across the main level (cleaning mode "mopping"), intended to run after a full vacuum pass has already picked up dry debris. Disables CleanGenius for deterministic control and always restores it. The persistent mop schedule is cleared only when the mop mode actually applied, the robot really started, and the run reached a real `completed` finish — so a rejected mode change, a no-op start, or an arrival-triggered return-to-base all keep the pending flag set to retry next run. |
| `script.x40_ultra_main_level_policy_clean` | X40 Ultra Deterministic Run (Full Floor Or Segment) | queued | THE single serialized entry (mode: queued) for every deterministic X40 run that toggles CleanGenius / cleaning mode — both the automatic full-floor pass and the one-room segment clean. Because every such run is an invocation of THIS one queued script, the queue serializes them atomically: no two runs can interleave their CleanGenius/mode changes, so no separate lock helper (and its non-atomic check-then-set) is needed. kind=full_floor (the default) vacuums the main level and adds a mop when one is pending or the last mop is >= 3 days old; kind=segment runs one vacuum-only segment via x40_ultra_segment_vacuum_only; kind=mop_only runs just the mop pass (x40_ultra_main_level_mop_only) for a floor whose vacuum pass already completed. The run is skipped entirely when the X40 is already busy with an external (manual/app) run, so we never disable CleanGenius or change the mode on a robot we are not driving. |
| `script.vacuum_main_level_full_floor` | Vacuum Main Level Full Floor | queued | Launch the main-level clean. Fire-and-forget: it starts the (long-running, self-observing) clean via script.turn_on and returns immediately, so callers such as vacuum_main_and_upstairs_levels start the upstairs robot and send trip notifications without waiting for the whole run. A forced mop launches the mop script directly; otherwise the policy decides. Routing on the force here (rather than a shared latch) keeps each request tied to its own queued run. |
| `script.vacuum_upstairs_full_floor` | Vacuum Upstairs Full Floor | single | Send the upstairs Valetudo vacuum to clean the full upstairs floor over MQTT. |
| `script.vacuum_main_and_upstairs_levels` | Vacuum Main And Upstairs Levels | queued | Run one full-floor cleaning pass on both resident levels. |
| `script.vacuum_master_bedroom` | Vacuum Master Bedroom | single | Send the upstairs Valetudo vacuum to clean the owner-suite bedroom segment. |
| `script.vacuum_guest_room` | Vacuum Guest Room | single | Send the upstairs Valetudo vacuum to clean the guest room segment. |
| `script.vacuum_bathroom` | Vacuum Bathroom | single | Send the upstairs Valetudo vacuum to clean the bathroom segment. |
| `script.vacuum_hallway` | Vacuum Hallway | single | Send the upstairs Valetudo vacuum to clean the hallway segment (entryway segment excluded because it does not work correctly). |
| `script.vacuum_kitchen` | Vacuum Kitchen | single | Send the main-level Dreame vacuum to clean the kitchen segment. |
| `script.vacuum_living_room` | Vacuum Living Room | single | Send the main-level Dreame vacuum to clean the living room segment. |
| `script.vacuum_office` | Vacuum Office | single | Send the upstairs Valetudo vacuum to clean the office segment. |
| `script.x40_ultra_segment_vacuum_only` | X40 Ultra Segment Vacuum Only | queued | Vacuum-only clean of one X40 map segment with CleanGenius deterministically disabled and the cleaning mode forced to `sweeping` first, so a leftover mopping mode can never put water down. Quiet suction by default. Invoked ONLY from x40_ultra_main_level_policy_clean (kind=segment) so it inherits that single queue's serialization and its at-rest entry guard; the raw dreame_vacuum.vacuum_clean_segment call alone does not establish sweeping and could mop under CleanGenius. |
| `script.vacuum_upstairs_segment_guarded` | Vacuum Upstairs Segment (Guarded) | queued | Shared launch boundary for upstairs (Valetudo) room cleans: recheck the guest veto immediately before delegating to the requested per-room segment script, so a guest arriving while a request waits in this queue is honored. Delegating to the existing per-room scripts keeps the segment maps in one place. After delegating it BLOCKS until the upstairs run reaches a terminal state, tracked via the Valetudo MQTT status topic (the trusted control channel, not the flaky upstairs Valetudo HA vacuum entity the config avoids by design). Because the per-room scripts are fire-and-forget, this hold plus mode: queued is what serializes upstairs room requests: a second room waits for the first run to finish instead of overwriting it mid-run. The upstairs robot is vacuum-only hardware, so this is a privacy boundary, not a mop one. |
| `script.vacuum_clean_room` | Vacuum One Room | queued | Dashboard room launcher: vacuum the one room named by the `room` field (an HA area id), vacuum-only. The room is a call-time field, never a shared helper, so a queued request can only ever clean the room that was tapped. Upstairs Valetudo rooms dispatch to the guarded upstairs boundary (that robot cannot mop); X40 rooms route through the single deterministic dispatcher (x40_ultra_main_level_policy_clean, kind=segment) so they serialize with automatic full-floor runs and force sweeping — a leftover mopping mode can never mop during a room run. Both are started with script.turn_on so each robot's own queue serializes its rooms while this launcher returns at once; a tap on an upstairs room is never stuck behind a main-level run. A blocked or unknown room sends a notification instead of failing silently. |
| `script.vacuum_manual_start` | Start Robot Vacuums | queued | Dashboard launcher for whole-floor runs: `robot` is main, upstairs, den, or all. Hands off to the same guarded scripts the automations use, so the guest veto, the den-door guard, and the X40's deterministic CleanGenius-off flow all still apply; the main level mops only when a mop is due, exactly like the automatic runs. Never calls vacuum.start or vacuum.clean_area directly. A blocked start (guest veto, or an open den door) sends a notification naming the reason instead of failing silently. |


## `packages/z2m_lifecycle.yaml`

### Automations

| ID | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `refresh_z2m_lifecycle_inventory` | refresh_z2m_lifecycle_inventory | single | Request a fresh Zigbee2MQTT device inventory at startup, every 30 minutes, and after bridge state changes or device removals. |
| `sync_z2m_decommission_options` | sync_z2m_decommission_options | restart | Keep the Z2M decommission dropdown's options in sync with the current lifecycle-issue device list. |
| `notify_z2m_lifecycle_issues` | notify_z2m_lifecycle_issues | restart | Raise or dismiss the Zigbee2MQTT lifecycle-issues persistent notification and notify everyone when the issue summary changes. |
| `handle_z2m_device_remove_response` | handle_z2m_device_remove_response | queued | Report the result of a Zigbee2MQTT device-remove request and refresh the inventory after a successful removal. |
| `reset_z2m_reboot_counter` | reset_z2m_reboot_counter | single | Reset manually from the recovery notification or after Zigbee2MQTT remains healthy for 10 minutes |
| `arm_z2m_host_watchdog_after_start` | arm_z2m_host_watchdog_after_start | restart | Hold the host/Proxmox shutdown watchdog disarmed for 20 minutes after every Home Assistant start. Zigbee2MQTT needs ~10-15 min to fully recover on this host after a reboot; without this grace period that normal recovery looks like a bridge failure and trips the watchdog (recovery restarts, and eventually rest_command.proxmox_shutdown). Also clears the reboot counter so a reboot that happened mid-recovery can't leave it pre-loaded toward escalation. The helper's `initial: false` means it is already disarmed the instant HA restarts (before any retained MQTT / early trigger can run the watchdog); this run only re-arms it 20 min later. |
| `reconcile_z2m_host_watchdog_armed` | reconcile_z2m_host_watchdog_armed | single | Reload-safe backstop for arm_z2m_host_watchdog_after_start. The helper can be left disarmed with no pending re-arm when a reload cancels the arming run mid-delay, or an input_boolean/full reload reapplies `initial: false`. A state *trigger's* `for:` timer would be lost the same way, so poll on a time_pattern and use state *conditions* (evaluated against last_changed each run). Re-arm when Zigbee2MQTT is fully healthy again (nothing left to protect - handles a reload during normal operation) or when it has simply been disarmed past the grace window (arming run was cancelled - a real outage must still be able to escalate). |
| `shutdown_proxmox_z2m_unavailable` | shutdown_proxmox_z2m_unavailable | single | Escalate bridge-wide Zigbee2MQTT outages while the host watchdog is armed: notify, restart the Z2M app (up to 3 times, not during OTA updates), then shut down the Proxmox host as a last resort. |

### Scripts

| Script | Alias | Mode | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `script.z2m_reset_reboot_counter` | Z2M - Reset Reboot Counter | single | Reset the Zigbee2MQTT watchdog reboot counter. |
| `script.z2m_decommission_selected_device` | Z2M - Decommission Selected Device | single | Decommission the device selected in the Z2M decommission dropdown. |
| `script.z2m_force_decommission_selected_device` | Z2M - Force Decommission Selected Device | single | Force-remove the device selected in the Z2M decommission dropdown, even if it is not responding. |
| `script.z2m_decommission_device` | Z2M - Decommission Device | single | Send a Zigbee2MQTT remove request for the selected device (optionally forced) and post a persistent notification about the request. |
